```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)
library(fastDummies)
library(caret)

# This is the precomputed data for predicting popularity, we are going to do an elastic net model,
# combined with a grid search to find the best alpha and lambda values. The grid search allows us to make a 
# MSE heatmap and remove the load of having a dynamic prediction model.
# We precompute everything because fitting hundreds of models in real time would be way too slow for a web app.

# Function to prepare data with top genres and artists
# We make this a function because we need to test many different combinations of genre/artist limits
# and we don't want to repeat the same data preparation code over and over
prepare_data <- function(top_n_genres, top_n_artists) {
  
  spotify <- read_csv("Spotify-2000.csv") %>%
    # Remove Index and Title because they don't predict popularity and would just add noise
    select(-Index, -Title) %>%
    # Log transformations for skewed variables - this is crucial because
    # Duration, Speechiness, and Liveness are heavily right-skewed, which can hurt model performance
    # Taking the log makes them more normally distributed, which works better with linear models
    mutate(
      `Log Duration`    = log(`Length (Duration)` + 1),  # +1 to avoid log(0) issues
      `Log Speechiness` = log(Speechiness + 1),
      `Log Liveness`    = log(Liveness + 1),
      # Create decade groups to capture temporal trends in music popularity
      # Different decades have different musical styles and popularity patterns
      decade_group = case_when(
        Year >= 1956 & Year <= 1969 ~ "Y1",
        Year >= 1970 & Year <= 1979 ~ "Y2",
        Year >= 1980 & Year <= 1989 ~ "Y3",
        Year >= 1990 & Year <= 1999 ~ "Y4",
        Year >= 2000 & Year <= 2009 ~ "Y5",
        Year >= 2010 & Year <= 2014 ~ "Y6",
        Year >= 2015 & Year <= 2019 ~ "Y7"
      )
    ) %>%
    # Create decade dummy variables with fast dummies so it is compatible with glmnet
    # We use fastDummies instead of model.matrix because it gives us more control
    # and doesn't automatically drop levels like model.matrix sometimes does
    fastDummies::dummy_cols(select_columns = "decade_group", remove_first_dummy = TRUE) %>%
    # Drop original variables that we've transformed or encoded
    # We keep the log versions and dummy versions, but remove the originals to avoid redundancy
    select(-c(Liveness, Speechiness, `Length (Duration)`, Year, decade_group))
  
  # Keep only top genres and artists to reduce dimensionality and focus on most important categories
  # This is important because having too many rare categories can lead to overfitting
  # and makes the model harder to interpret
  top_genres  <- spotify %>% count(`Top Genre`, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = top_n_genres) %>% pull(`Top Genre`)
  top_artists <- spotify %>% count(Artist, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = top_n_artists) %>% pull(Artist)
  
  # Replace rare genres/artists with "Other" to reduce the number of categories
  # This prevents the model from overfitting to artists/genres that only appear a few times
  spotify <- spotify %>%
    mutate(
      `Top Genre` = if_else(`Top Genre` %in% top_genres, `Top Genre`, "Other"),
      Artist      = if_else(Artist      %in% top_artists, Artist,      "Other")
    )
  
  # Clean column names to make them R-friendly and glmnet-compatible
  names(spotify) <- make.names(names(spotify))
  
  # Scale numeric variables
  # Scaling is important for regularized models like elastic net because
  # variables with larger scales would otherwise dominate the penalty terms
  # we don't scale the target variable popularity or dummy variables which are already 0/1
  numeric_cols <- sapply(spotify, is.numeric)
  dummy_cols <- grepl("decade_group_", names(spotify))
  cols_to_scale <- numeric_cols & !dummy_cols & names(spotify) != "Popularity"
  
  spotify_scaled <- spotify
  # We use scale function which,puts all numeric variables on the same scale, making regularization fair
  spotify_scaled[cols_to_scale] <- scale(spotify[cols_to_scale])
  
  return(spotify_scaled)
}

# Function to run elastic net with best alpha for given data
# We make this a function because we need to run the same model fitting process
# for every combination of genre/artist in our grid search
run_elastic_net <- function(spotify_data) {
  
  # We build the formula to include all variables except Popularity
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste("Popularity ~", paste(names(spotify_data)[-which(names(spotify_data) == "Popularity")], collapse = " + ")))
  # model.matrix converts factors to dummy variables
  model_matrix <- model.matrix(model_formula, data = spotify_data)[, -1]
  
  # We use 70% for training and 30% for testing
  set.seed(123)
  trainIndex <- createDataPartition(spotify_data$Popularity, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
  X_train <- model_matrix[trainIndex, ]
  y_train <- spotify_data$Popularity[trainIndex]
  X_test <- model_matrix[-trainIndex, ]
  y_test <- spotify_data$Popularity[-trainIndex]
  
  # Test different alpha values to find the best one
  # We test 5 values to balance computational cost with finding a good alpha
  alphas <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)  # Just 5 alpha values for speed
  rmse_values <- numeric(length(alphas))
  
  # For each alpha, we do cross validation to find the best lambda
  # Then we test that model on our holdout test set to get an unbiased RMSE
  set.seed(123)
  for(i in 1:length(alphas)) {
    cv_model <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = alphas[i])
    predictions <- predict(cv_model, s = cv_model$lambda.min, newx = X_test)
    rmse_values[i] <- sqrt(mean((predictions - y_test)^2))
  }
  
  # Find best alpha and train final model
  # We pick the alpha that gave us the lowest RMSE on the test set, because we want an accurate prediction
  # of popularity, and mse is a good measure of prediction error
  best_alpha_idx <- which.min(rmse_values)
  best_alpha <- alphas[best_alpha_idx]
  best_rmse <- rmse_values[best_alpha_idx]
  
  # Calculate R-squared for best model
  cv_model_best <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = best_alpha)
  predictions_best <- predict(cv_model_best, s = cv_model_best$lambda.min, newx = X_test)
  SSE <- sum((predictions_best - y_test)^2)
  SST <- sum((y_test - mean(y_test))^2)
  r_squared <- 1 - (SSE / SST)
  
  # Count variables selected
  coeffs <- coef(cv_model_best, s = cv_model_best$lambda.min)
  num_vars_selected <- sum(coeffs[,1] != 0) - 1
  
  #use return list to return multiple values
  return(list(
    best_alpha = best_alpha,
    best_lambda = cv_model_best$lambda.min,
    best_rmse = best_rmse,
    r_squared = r_squared,
    num_vars_selected = num_vars_selected,
    total_vars = ncol(model_matrix),
    num_genres = length(unique(spotify_data$Top.Genre)),
    num_artists = length(unique(spotify_data$Artist)),
    coefficients = coeffs,  
    cv_model = cv_model_best
  ))
}

# We test fewer combinations to keep computation time short
genre_thresholds <- c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20)  
artist_thresholds <- c(1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15)

# Making a list to store results for our R shiny app
results_list <- list()
coefficients_storage <- list()  
counter <- 1

# Print progress information so we know the model is runnig
cat("Starting grid search...\n")
cat("Testing", length(genre_thresholds), "genre limits x", length(artist_thresholds), "artist limits =", 
    length(genre_thresholds) * length(artist_thresholds), "combinations\n\n")

#grid search over genre and artist limits
for(g in genre_thresholds) {
  for(a in artist_thresholds) {
    
    # Print progress so we can see how long this is taking
    cat("Testing: Top", g, "genres, Top", a, "artists\n")
    
    spotify_data <- prepare_data(g, a)
    
    # Run elastic net with this data configuration
    result <- run_elastic_net(spotify_data)
    
    # Store coefficients with a unique key, so it can be accessed later
    combo_key <- paste0("G", g, "_A", a)
    coefficients_storage[[combo_key]] <- result$coefficients
    
    # Storing the results in a structured format
    results_list[[counter]] <- data.frame(
      Genre_Limit = g,
      Artist_Limit = a,
      Best_Alpha = round(result$best_alpha, 3),
      Best_Lambda = round(result$best_lambda, 6), 
      RMSE = round(result$best_rmse, 4),
      R_Squared = round(result$r_squared, 4),
      Vars_Selected = result$num_vars_selected,
      Total_Vars = result$total_vars,
      Num_Genres = result$num_genres,
      Num_Artists = result$num_artists,
      Combo_Key = combo_key
    )
    
    counter <- counter + 1
  }
}

# Combineing all results into a single data frame
final_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

#filtering for lowest mse and R2
best_rmse_idx <- which.min(final_results$RMSE)
best_r2_idx <- which.max(final_results$R_Squared)

# Print summary
# We use cat() instead of print() for a nicer look at the data
cat("\n" %>% rep(3) %>% paste(collapse = ""))  # Print 3 blank lines
cat("=== GRID SEARCH COMPLETE ===\n")
cat("Total combinations tested:", nrow(final_results), "\n\n")

cat("=== BEST RMSE ===\n")
cat("Top", final_results$Genre_Limit[best_rmse_idx], "genres, Top", final_results$Artist_Limit[best_rmse_idx], "artists\n")
cat("RMSE:", final_results$RMSE[best_rmse_idx], "\n")
cat("R-squared:", final_results$R_Squared[best_rmse_idx], "\n")
cat("Alpha:", final_results$Best_Alpha[best_rmse_idx], "\n")
cat("Variables selected:", final_results$Vars_Selected[best_rmse_idx], "out of", final_results$Total_Vars[best_rmse_idx], "\n\n")

cat("=== BEST R-SQUARED ===\n")
cat("Top", final_results$Genre_Limit[best_r2_idx], "genres, Top", final_results$Artist_Limit[best_r2_idx], "artists\n")
cat("RMSE:", final_results$RMSE[best_r2_idx], "\n")
cat("R-squared:", final_results$R_Squared[best_r2_idx], "\n")
cat("Alpha:", final_results$Best_Alpha[best_r2_idx], "\n")
cat("Variables selected:", final_results$Vars_Selected[best_r2_idx], "out of", final_results$Total_Vars[best_r2_idx], "\n\n")

#Shows us everything of the best configuration
best_combo_key <- final_results$Combo_Key[best_rmse_idx]
best_coeffs <- coefficients_storage[[best_combo_key]]
# Only show non-zero coefficients
nonzero_coeffs <- best_coeffs[best_coeffs[,1] != 0, , drop = FALSE]

cat("\n=== COEFFICIENTS FOR BEST MODEL ===\n")
cat("Combination:", best_combo_key, "\n")
print(nonzero_coeffs)

save(final_results, coefficients_storage, file = "grid_search_results.RData")
write_csv(final_results, "grid_search_results.csv")
cat("\nResults saved to 'grid_search_results.RData' and 'grid_search_results.csv'\n")

# Display the full results dataframe for reference
# This shows all combinations and their performance, useful for creating heatmaps
cat("\n=== ALL RESULTS ===\n")
print(final_results)
```
